purpose: Extends WP 6.9+ cache salt system to image conversion status, activity log queries, and telemetry audit results for granular settings-aware cache invalidation.
riskRationale: Changes are well-contained, follow established patterns, use function_exists() gates for backward compatibility, and include proper fallback paths. No security concerns identified.

text: The implementation correctly follows the established Database_Cleanup::get_counts() pattern across three new classes with SALT_KEY constants, function_exists() gates, and transient fallbacks. The code is clean, consistent, and properly invalidates caches on relevant data writes. One architectural inconsistency exists in how Telemetry's audit salt is bumped from Main.

reasoning: All changes are functionally correct, backward-compatible, and well-integrated. The single architectural concern is minor and does not block merge.

message: Well-designed public invalidate_img_info_cache() method that encapsulates salt management logic cleanly, allowing Main::on_settings_update() to call it without knowing the internal salt key name.
The old fallback version-bump code is preserved inline alongside the new salt bump, ensuring zero regression on WP < 6.9.
The single $has_salted boolean check at the top of scan() avoids repeated function_exists() calls and keeps the branching logic clean.

AUDIT_SALT_KEY is declared as private const, forcing Main::on_settings_update() to duplicate the salt option name as a raw string literal ('wppo_audit_salt') rather than using a class API. This creates two maintenance points and is inconsistent with the Img_Converter pattern where Main calls invalidate_img_info_cache().
suggestion: Add a public static Telemetry::invalidate_audit_cache() method (mirroring Img_Converter::invalidate_img_info_cache()) and call it from Main::on_settings_update() instead of directly manipulating the option.

message: The function_exists('wp_cache_get_salted') check here is redundant if Telemetry::invalidate_audit_cache() gates internally. On WP < 6.9, the wppo_audit_salt option is never read, making this a no-op that creates an orphan option entry.
suggestion: Remove the outer function_exists() guard once the proposed Telemetry::invalidate_audit_cache() method is in place, as it will handle the WP version gate internally.
